original_prompt_answer: The Transformer adds positional encodings to its input embeddings so that the model receives information about the relative or absolute positions of tokens in a sequence, thereby providing the necessary order information that the architecture itself does not capture  [Source: data/NIPS-2017-attention-is-all-you-need-Paper.pdf, Page: 6].
refined_coverage_answer: The Transformer adds positional encodings to the input embeddings so that the model receives information about the **relative or absolute positions of tokens in a sequence**—a necessary step because the architecture itself (which relies on self‑attention rather than recurrence or convolution) has no inherent notion of token order [Source: data/NIPS-2017-attention-is-all-you-need-Paper.pdf, Page: 6].

original_prompt_answer: Acknowledging a partner’s feelings after an argument shows respect and lets them know they have been heard.  When you recognize that something you said or did upset them and offer an apology, it makes the other person feel respected, heard, and reassured that you are trying to repair the situation, which in turn strengthens the relationship [Source: data/amity_relationship_care.pdf, Page: 23].  This act of acknowledgment is described as a “communication super‑power” that helps move the couple toward repair and rebuilding trust [Source: data/amity_relationship_care.pdf, Page: 23].
refined_coverage_answer: Acknowledging a partner’s feelings after an argument is important because it shows respect, makes the partner feel heard, and signals that you are trying to repair the situation. When you acknowledge how the other person is feeling, they experience respect and the sense that you care enough to recognize their hurt, which helps strengthen the relationship and move toward resolution [Source: data/amity_relationship_care.pdf, Page: 23] [Source: data/amity_relationship_care.pdf, Page: 23]
